Plot and report the main effects from a Bayesian mixed model

Source: R/bayes_mm_mainFX.R
bayes_mm_mainFX.Rd

For each main effect (condition) in the model, prints a table of the estimated means and contrasts, and draws a plot showing the observed data and the posterior distributions of the estimated means. Any arguments of eyethinkdata::pirateye() can be passed in to change the plot.

Usage

bayes_mm_mainFX(
  bmm,
  mainfxs = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  contrast_sparkline = F,
  show_mpe = T,
  show_preddist = T,
  ...
)

Arguments

bmm

A model from bayes_mm_run() (or the list returned by bayes_mm()).

mainfxs

A vector of the names of the conditions to plot. By default all of the main effects in the model are plotted.

title

Extra text for the title of the plot (and the file name).

contrast_sparkline

Show the distribution of the contrast estimate below the plot?

show_mpe

Write the MPEs on the plot?

show_preddist

Show the posterior distributions of the means?

...

Further arguments for eyethinkdata::pirateye(), eg bars = TRUE, violin = FALSE, w and h (the width and height of the saved pdf).

Value

A list with plot_mainfx, the plot (a cowplot grid, so you can also draw it with print()), and data_mainfx, a list of the data behind it: observed, predicted (the posterior samples), m (the estimated means), mpe and bcontrasts.

Details

For conditions that are factors, the plot shows the observed data (violins), the estimated mean for each level, and the posterior distribution of each estimate (the smaller violins). When a condition has two levels, the MPE (maximum probability of effect, ie the probability that the difference between the two is not zero) is written between the two levels. The MPE is the pd (probability of direction) from the modelbased package.

With contrast_sparkline = TRUE, the distribution of the difference between conditions is drawn underneath, with the central 95% shaded in grey and zero marked by a black line. If the line is outside of the grey area, there is more than a 95% probability that the difference is not zero.

For conditions that are continuous variables, a separate plot shows the predicted line, with the MPE for the slope.

The text output is printed to the console. (When the function is called by bayes_mm() it is saved to a file.) Plots are saved as pdfs by eyethinkdata::pirateye(): to change where, pass outp in ... (use outp = "" to not save them).

For binomial models the means are on the probability scale.

See also

bayes_mm(), bayes_mm_interact(), eyethinkdata::pirateye()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
mfx <- bayes_mm_mainFX(bmm, mainfxs = "adcon")
mfx$plot_mainfx
bayes_mm_mainFX(bmm, mainfxs = c("adcon", "tv"), bars = TRUE, violin = FALSE,
                contrast_sparkline = TRUE, show_mpe = FALSE)
} # }
